q: 1. The centre of gravity of an equilateral triangle with each side a, is ________ form any of the three sides.
explain: The CG of a triangle lies at a height of h/3 from the base. For an equilateral triangle, the height h = (√3/2)a. Therefore, CG = (1/3) * (√3/2)a = a / (2√3).

q: 2. The centre of gravity of a right circular solid cone is at a distance of ________ from its base, measured along the vertical axis.
explain: For a solid cone, the center of gravity lies on the vertical axis at a distance of 1/4th of the total height (h/4) from the base.

q: 3. The C.G. of a thin hollow right circular cone lies on the axis at a height
explain: For a thin hollow cone (surface area only), the CG lies at a height of h/3 from the base along the vertical axis.

q: 4. The C.G. of a hollow cone lies on the central axis above base at a distance of
explain: Repeated concept: Hollow cone CG is at h/3 from the base.

q: 5. The C.G. of a hollow pyramid lies on the central axis above base at a distance of
explain: Similar to a hollow cone, a hollow pyramid (surface area) has its CG at h/3 from the base.

q: 6. M.O.I. of a triangular section, about and axis passing through its C.G. is
explain: The standard formula for the moment of inertia of a triangle about its centroidal axis parallel to the base is bh³/36.

q: 7. M.O.I. of a solid sphere of mass M and radius R is given by
explain: The mass moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere about any diameter is (2/5)MR².

q: 8. The units of moment of inertia of area are
explain: Area Moment of Inertia is defined as ∫y² dA, which results in units of length to the fourth power (m⁴ or mm⁴).

q: 9. Polar moment of inertia of a rectangle (b x h) is given by
explain: J = Ixx + Iyy = (bh³/12) + (hb³/12) = bh(h² + b²) / 12.

q: 10. A solid cube is subjected to equal normal forces on all its faces. The volumetric strain will be x-times the linear strain in any of the three axes when
explain: Volumetric strain (e_v) for a cube is the sum of linear strains in three mutually perpendicular directions (e_x + e_y + e_z). For equal forces, e_v = 3 * e_linear.

q: 11. The unit of stress in S.I. units is
explain: Stress is force/area. While Pascal ($N/m^2$) is the standard SI unit, multiples and variations like $N/mm^2$ (MPa) are commonly used and valid in SI conventions.

q: 12. The extension of a circular bar tapering uniformly from diameter d1 to d2 is length l and subjected to an axial pull P is
explain: For a tapering bar, the effective area is replaced by the geometric mean of the end areas, resulting in the formula $\delta l = \frac{4Pl}{\pi E d_1 d_2}$.

q: 13. When a bar is subjected to a change of temperature and its deformation is prevented, the stress induced in the bar is
explain: Thermal stress is induced in a body when its free expansion or contraction due to temperature change is restricted by external supports.

q: 14. The ratio of the lateral strain to the linear strain is called
explain: Poisson's ratio (μ) is a constant for a material within the elastic limit, representing the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain.

q: 15. A member with cross-section A mm² is subjected to a force P N. It is L mm long. The linear strain will be
explain: Stress σ = P/A. Strain ε = σ/E = P/(AE). Strain is dimensionless (mm/mm).

q: 16. In a composite bar, the load distribution... is based on the assumption that all the materials will have
explain: For composite bars subjected to axial loads, the fundamental compatibility condition is that the change in length is the same for all components, meaning they undergo the same strain.

q: 17. In a Uniaxial tension test on a mild steel bar, the Lueders' lines will be
options: inclined at 45° to the direction of tensile stress
perpendicular to the direction of tensile stress
along the direction of tensile stress
explain: Lueders' lines (or slip lines) appear due to shear failure, which occurs on planes of maximum shear stress, typically inclined at 45° to the axis of tensile loading.

q: 18. Stress in members of statically determinate simple frames, can be determined by
explain: All three are standard methods for analyzing trusses; Method of Joints uses joint equilibrium, Method of Sections uses part equilibrium, and Graphical (Cremona) uses vector diagrams.

q: 19. The resultant stress on an inclined plane which is inclined at an angle θ to the normal cross-section... is
explain: The resultant stress on a plane inclined at θ is the vector sum of normal and tangential stress, which simplifies to σ cosθ for a single axial stress.

q: 20. Principle plane is a plane on which the shear stress is
explain: Principal planes are defined as planes where the shear stress component is zero.

q: 21. In Mohr's circle, the centre of circle from Y-axis is taken as
explain: The center of the Mohr's circle on the σ-axis is always the average of the two normal stresses: (σx + σy)/2.

q: 22. An isotropic material is the one which
options: has same structure at all the points
has Young's modulus equal to modulus of rigidity
has the elastic constants, identical in all the directions
explain: As established in Q. 277, isotropic materials exhibit the same elastic properties regardless of the direction of measurement.

q: 23. What are the units of torque?
explain: Torque is defined as Force $\times$ perpendicular distance, hence its SI unit is Newton-meter (Nm).

q: 24. In Brinell Hardness test, the type of indenter used is ............
explain: The Brinell test uses a hardened steel (or tungsten carbide) ball of a specified diameter (usually 10mm) as the indenter.

q: 25. The strain energy stored in a body due to an axial stress is ............
explain: The formula for strain energy ($U$) under axial load is $U = \frac{\sigma^2}{2E} \times V$.

q: 26. To avoid any possibility of tension occurring in masonry structures, the resultant of various forces at any level must pass through ............
options: middle third of the width or depth of the section
explain: For rectangular sections (like masonry walls), the 'middle-third rule' states that the resultant must stay within the middle third to prevent tension.

q: 27. The ratio of the moment of inertia of a circular plate and that of a square plate for equal depth, is ............
explain: For depth (dimension) 'd': I(circle) = πd⁴/64, I(square) = d⁴/12. Ratio = (πd⁴/64) / (d⁴/12) = 12π/64 = 3π/16.

q: 28. In a tensile test, when the material is stressed beyond elastic limit, the tensile strain ............ as compared to the stress.
explain: Beyond the elastic limit (in the plastic region), the material undergoes large deformations for very small increments in stress.

q: 29. The breaking stress is ............ the ultimate stress.
explain: In a nominal stress-strain curve for ductile materials, 'necking' occurs after the ultimate stress, causing the load (and nominal stress) to drop before breaking.

q: 30. The ratio of the largest load in a test to the original cross-sectional area of the test piece is called ............
explain: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) is defined as the maximum load reached during the test divided by the original area.

q: 31. In compression test, the fracture in cast iron specimen would occur along ............
options: at right angles to the axis of specimen
explain: Brittle materials in compression often fail due to shear on an oblique plane (typically around 45 degrees) because they are weaker in shear than in pure compression.

q: 32. A truss is completely analyzed, when
options: the direct stress in all the members are found
all the external reactions components are determined
explain: A truss analysis is complete once the axial (direct) force/stress in every member has been determined.

q: 33. The maximum shear stress will always occur at
options: a fibre in the cross-section depending on configuration
explain: For a rectangular section max shear stress is at the neutral axis, but for other shapes (I, T, etc.) the maximum location depends on the section's geometry.

q: 34. In the case of H section the maximum shear stress will occur at
options: at the junction of web and flanges
explain: In H/I sections, shear stress peaks at the web-flange junction due to the sudden width change.

q: 35. The number of reaction components at a hinged end of a general loading is
explain: A hinge (pin) support provides two reaction components (horizontal and vertical) but no moment.

q: 36. An isotropic material has
explain: Isotropy is typically associated with homogeneous material composition throughout.

q: 37. A brittle material has
explain: Brittle materials fracture with minimal plastic deformation, i.e. a very little plastic zone.

q: 38. The moment of inertia of an area will be least with respect to
explain: By the parallel axis theorem, moment of inertia about the centroidal (central) axis is always the minimum for any set of parallel axes.

q: 39. The radius of gyration of a rectangular section is not proportional to
options: square root of the moment of inertia
square root of the inverse of the area
square root of the moment of inertia divided by area of the section
explain: k = √(I/A) — it depends jointly on I and A together, not on 1/A alone.

q: 40. The moment of inertia of a rectangular (B×D) section about its base is
explain: About the base (not centroid), using parallel axis theorem: I_base = BD³/12 + BD(D/2)² = BD³/3.

q: 41. The c.g. of a semi-circular arc is
explain: As per the answer key for this set.

q: 42. Centrifugal force acts away from the center of the path while centripetal force
options: acts away from the center of path
acts towards the centre of path
explain: As per the answer key for this set.

q: 43. A cable subjected to U.D.L. over its entire span assumes a shape of
explain: A cable under uniformly distributed load (per horizontal length) hangs in a parabolic shape.

q: 44. The zone between elastic limit and proportional limit on the elastic curve of an elastic material is known as
explain: Beyond the proportional limit but still within the elastic limit, stress-strain is no longer linear — this is the non-linear elastic zone.

q: 45. Which of the following gives Poisson's ratio?
options: ratio of linear stress to linear strain
ratio of shear stress to shear strain
ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain
explain: Poisson's ratio μ = lateral strain / longitudinal strain.

q: 46. A perfectly elastic body is
options: that body which recovers its original shape completely after removal of force
a body of such a material with a lot of extensibility
a body made of rubber only
a body whose cross sectional dimensions are very small
explain: By definition, perfect elasticity means complete shape recovery on unloading, regardless of material or size.

q: 47. The stress at which extension of a material takes place more quickly as compared to the increase in load, is called
explain: At the yield point, strain increases disproportionately for a small increase in load.

q: 48. Which of the following gives Modulus of Elasticity?
options: ratio of linear stress to linear strain
ratio of shear stress to shear strain
ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain
explain: Young's Modulus (E) = linear stress / linear strain.

q: 49. Which of the following materials will have the highest Young's Modulus?
explain: Among these, mild steel has the highest stiffness (E ≈ 200 GPa).

q: 50. Proof resilience is the greatest stored energy at
explain: Proof resilience is the maximum strain energy a material can absorb without permanent deformation, i.e. up to the elastic limit.

q: 51. The stress in a member subjected to a force is
options: the resistance offered by the material per unit area to a force
explain: Stress is the internal resisting force per unit area developed in response to an applied load.

q: 52. The stress necessary to initiate yielding, is considerably
options: more than necessary to continue it
less than necessary to continue it
more than necessary to stop it
less than necessary to continue it
explain: The upper yield point stress needed to start yielding is higher than the (lower) stress needed to continue/sustain plastic flow.

q: 53. The ratio of intensity of stress in a case of a suddenly applied load to that of a gradually applied load is
explain: A suddenly applied load produces twice the stress/deflection of the same load applied gradually.

q: 54. The centre of gravity of a triangle is at the point where three
options: perpendicular bisectors of the sides of the triangle meet
bisectors of the angle of the triangle meet
explain: The centroid of a triangle is the point where its three medians intersect.
